capabilities.text: Nurse logs in with existing hospital credentials
capabilities.quote: When a nurse on Ward 4 opens the tool, they first log in using their existing hospital credentials—no new password needed.

capabilities.text: Form shows patient name and ID from OmniCare
capabilities.quote: Then they see a simple form that pulls the patient’s name and ID from OmniCare automatically.

capabilities.text: Nurse saves a note once to OmniCare and the spreadsheet
capabilities.quote: Their first step is to type the note into the blank text box, just like they do now, but now it’s only once.

capabilities.text: Ward manager views notes in spreadsheet
capabilities.quote: The ward manager needs to view the notes daily to track patient progress and staff workload

capabilities.text: Finance imports a complete weekly spreadsheet of patient notes
capabilities.quote: They need to see each patient’s note clearly linked to the nurse who wrote it and the time it was entered—no missing or duplicated entries.

capabilities.text: Nurse sees a note saved in OmniCare but not yet in the spreadsheet
capabilities.quote: If the file was locked, she’d see a red warning that the note is saved in OmniCare but not yet in the spreadsheet

capabilities.text: Ward manager sees the morning count check
capabilities.quote: and she checks the total number of entries matches the number of nurses on shift.

capabilities.text: Nurse sees a pending message until a note is in both systems
capabilities.quote: The note appears instantly in OmniCare under the patient’s record. Then, at 7:30 AM the next day, the tool automatically writes it to the spreadsheet

capabilities.text: Patient name and ID appear within two seconds of selection
capabilities.quote: Default: they show within two seconds of her selecting the patient

capabilities.text: Nurse sees a green confirmation message within two seconds of saving a note
capabilities.quote: She clicks Save & Send, and sees a green confirmation: “Note saved in OmniCare and scheduled for spreadsheet.”

capabilities.text: Tool pushes note to OmniCare and spreadsheet in one click
capabilities.quote: She finishes the note, click “Save & Send,” and the tool pushes it to both OmniCare and the spreadsheet in one click—no extra steps.

capabilities.text: Ward manager sees notes clearly labeled with patient name, time, and nurse’s name
capabilities.quote: the spreadsheet must be formatted so that each note is clearly labeled with the patient name, time, and nurse’s name

capabilities.text: Spreadsheet file saved and shared automatically by 7:30 AM each day
capabilities.quote: and the file must be saved and shared automatically by 7:30 AM each day.

capabilities.text: Finance checks that all notes from the previous week are present and properly dated
capabilities.quote: When they open the file, they check first that all 15 notes from the previous week are present and properly dated

capabilities.text: Finance imports the file directly into their cost calculation tool
capabilities.quote: I’ve asked them to confirm they can import the file directly into their cost calculation tool

capabilities.text: Spreadsheet saved as a CSV with a consistent format
capabilities.quote: so we’ll make sure it’s saved as a CSV with a consistent format.

capabilities.text: Tool generates one clean, complete entry per note
capabilities.quote: So the tool should generate one clean, complete entry per note and push it to the spreadsheet at the end of each shift.

capabilities.text: Tool must not run on the nurse’s personal device
capabilities.quote: the tool must not run on the nurse’s personal device—it must be accessed through the hospital’s desktop kiosks

capabilities.text: Tool must work on Windows 10 with Internet Explorer 11 compatibility
capabilities.quote: The developer must ensure the tool works on Windows 10 with Internet Explorer 11 compatibility

capabilities.text: Data must be stored in UK-based cloud servers
capabilities.quote: all data must be stored in UK-based cloud servers.

capabilities.text: Encrypt data in transit and at rest
capabilities.quote: we’ll also need to encrypt both in transit and at rest

capabilities.text: Keep access logs for audit purposes
capabilities.quote: and ensure that access logs are kept for audit purposes.

capabilities.text: Tool runs on a single cloud instance
capabilities.quote: The tool will run on a single cloud instance with moderate memory and processing

capabilities.text: Budget of around £10,000 for the full project
capabilities.quote: We have a budget of around £10,000 for the full project—covering the developer’s time, testing, and cloud hosting for the first year.

capabilities.text: First version working by the end of next quarter (October 31)
capabilities.quote: We need the first version working by the end of next quarter—around October 31.
